author: William Shakespeare
title: The Works of William Shakespeare, Cambridge Edition, Volume VIII: Hamlet, the 1603 quarto of Hamlet, King Lear and Othello
edition: Edited by William George Clark and William Aldis Wright; London and Cambridge: Macmillan and Co., 1866, Volume VIII. Project Gutenberg 49008. The library holds every play of the volume in printed order, each under its own headings: Hamlet (title, Dramatis Personae, Acts I to V), the reprint of the 1603 quarto, The Tragicall Historie of HAMLET Prince of Denmarke (scenes i to xviii as the editors bracket them), King Lear (title, Dramatis Personae, Acts I to V) and Othello (title, Dramatis Personae, Acts I to V), with every scene heading, speech and stage direction. The editors' title page, contents, Preface and Addenda, the Notes after Hamlet, King Lear and Othello, and the footnoted textual apparatus are omitted as editorial matter. Footnote anchors, variant readings and page and line numbers omitted; HTML emphasis flattened and horizontal indentation normalized. Speech boundaries, stage directions and the transcription's displayed verse and prose line breaks retained; the quarto's numbered speech prefixes (1., 2.) are the edition's own. An existing dotted lacuna belongs to this printed edition, not to the selection editor. Three plain-text note references the transcription types into the verse are removed: [619] after Hamlet's “I do not know,”, [284, 285] in King Lear and [8, 9] in Othello. One transcription error is corrected: in Hamlet, Act I, scene V, Gutenberg's “0 villain” (digit zero) is printed here as “O villain.” King Lear, Act I, was collated on 2026-11-18 word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive shakespeareworks08claruoft (this 1866 volume), each difference decided on its page images: two readings changed: Kent’s “I’ll tell thee thou dost evil” in Act I, scene I (page 165), which the transcription gives as “them dost evil”, and Edmund’s “fine word, ‘legitimate!’” in scene II, where it omits the space after the comma. King Lear, Acts II and III, and Othello, Act I, were collated on 2026-11-18 the same way: one reading changed, Cassio’s “as I may divine:” in Othello, Act I, scene II (page 448), where the transcription has a semicolon (the same speech’s two curly apostrophes were made straight like the rest), and the opening bracket of “[Exit Cornwall, led by Regan.” in King Lear, Act III, scene VII (page 361), which the transcription left at the end of Cornwall’s speech, was moved back to the stage direction. King Lear, Acts IV and V, and Othello, Acts II and III, were collated on 2026-11-18 the same way: four readings changed in King Lear, “The wretch that thou hast blown” in Act IV, scene I (page 363), which the transcription gives as “them hast blown”, and three commas it omits, in “Now fare you well, good sir.” and “had he been where he thought,” in Act IV, scene VI (page 382) and “fordone themselves,” in Act V, scene III (page 424); the one curly apostrophe of “unnumber’d” in Act IV, scene VI, was made straight like the rest, and Othello needed no change.

rights.basis: The selected English text is from the identified Macmillan 1866 Cambridge edition, published before 1931 and public domain in the United States as of 2026. Project Gutenberg explicitly lists this edition as public domain in the USA; its dated title page identifies the print text. Modern site boilerplate and apparatus are excluded.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg HTML (pglaf mirror of ebook 49008, pg49008-images.html). Kept four spans of the volume in order: from the HAMLET. heading to the first NOTES. heading, from The Tragicall Historie of HAMLET Prince of Denmarke. to KING LEAR., from KING LEAR. to the following NOTES. heading, and from OTHELLO. to the following NOTES. heading. Removed page numbers, line numbers, footnote anchors and the footnote divisions; play titles became level-1 headings, Dramatis Personae and act titles level-2 and scene titles level-3 headings; centred stage directions and Dramatis Personae lines became paragraphs; each stanza division (one speech) became a stanza block with a line per HTML line break; runs of ASCII whitespace collapsed to one space (no-break spaces kept), emphasis and small capitals flattened; the three plain-text note references removed and 'O villain' printed for the transcription's digit zero, as the edition note states. On 2026-11-18 blocks 2216 (“them dost evil” to “thou dost evil”) and 2257 (a space restored after “fine word,”) were corrected after collating King Lear, Act I, against the page images of IA shakespeareworks08claruoft. On 2026-11-18 seven of the editors' lettered textual notes that the first conversion had kept as paragraphs after the Dramatis Personae ([A] and [B] for Hamlet, [C] for King Lear, [D] to [G] for Othello) were removed as part of the omitted apparatus. On 2026-11-18 blocks 2957 (“them hast” to “thou hast”), 3095 and 3099 (a comma restored after “well” and after “thought”), 3403 (“themselves.” to “themselves,”) and 3091 (a curly apostrophe made straight) were corrected after collating King Lear, Acts IV and V, against the same page images.
